title: How to be a Great Team
blurb: How kitchen, bar, front of house, housekeeping and management work together through communication, mucking in and looking after each other.
siteNotes: How each department passes heads-ups to the others on a shift (radio, handover, huddle)
Who to speak to if a colleague seems to be struggling
legalNotes: From BHB-10MT-51. No legal rules are stated; this is good practice for working together.

cards.title: How to be a Great Team
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- explain why a busy night depends on every department
- share a heads-up quickly and clearly
- muck in, stay reliable and look after colleagues

cards.title: Hospitality is a team sport
cards.body:
On a busy night, no one gets through it alone. It takes the kitchen, the bar, front of house, housekeeping and management all pulling in the same direction.

When the team clicks, work is more enjoyable, service is better, and guests can feel the good atmosphere.

cards.title: Share it, do not assume
cards.body:
Share information clearly so everyone can adjust. A quick heads-up between departments prevents most of the little disasters that make a shift stressful.

> Do not assume someone else knows. Tell them.

items.title: Low on a dish
items.text: Tell the pass and front of house.

items.title: Big group in
items.text: A large party just walked in.

cards.title: Help where it is needed
cards.body: When it is slammed, jump in and help where it is needed, even if it is "not your job".

cards.title: Turn up, ready to work
cards.body:
Turn up on time, ready to work, so your colleagues are not left covering for you.

> Reliability is one of the most respected qualities in any team.

items.title: Turn up on time
items.text: Be there when the shift starts.

items.title: Colleagues not covering
items.text: Nobody left short because of you.

cards.title: A team that supports each other
cards.body:
Give and take feedback positively, treat everyone with respect, and celebrate the wins together. Notice when a colleague is struggling or having a rough day.

A team that supports each other handles pressure better and sticks together. We succeed, or struggle, together.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Tell people what is happening, do not assume they know
- A quick heads-up between departments prevents little disasters
- Muck in when it is busy, even if it is "not your job"
- Turn up on time and ready to work
- Look after each other and keep feedback positive

cards.q: On a busy night, no one gets through it alone.
cards.why: Service needs the kitchen, bar, front of house, housekeeping and management all pulling in the same direction.

cards.q: A table in your section is running late and the kitchen is about to plate their starters. What is most useful to do?
options: Tell the kitchen straight away so they can adjust
Say nothing, as the kitchen will notice in time
Mention it at the end of service as a learning
Ask the guests to hurry up their arrival
cards.why: Sharing a table running late, a low dish or a big group lets everyone adjust. Do not assume someone else knows.

cards.q: The restaurant is slammed and the pass is backing up. A great team member will:
options: Watch others struggle until asked
Muck in and help where needed
Take a break while it is busy
Stick strictly to their own job
cards.why: When it is slammed, you jump in and help, such as running a plate or clearing a table.

cards.q: Being reliable means turning up on time, ready to work.
cards.why: Turning up on time and ready means your colleagues are not left covering for you.

cards.q: A colleague points out a mistake in how you laid a table. Feedback should be given and taken:
options: Defensively, to protect your pride
Not at all, to avoid awkwardness
Positively, by both people
Only when a manager is present
cards.why: Giving and taking feedback positively is part of looking after each other.

cards.q: A quick heads-up between departments prevents many little disasters.
cards.why: A short heads-up stops the small problems that make a shift stressful.

cards.q: Which is one way to look after each other in a team?
options: Keep your head down on your own tasks
Leave personal worries to others
Give feedback only when it is going wrong
Notice when someone is struggling
cards.why: Looking after each other includes noticing a colleague who is struggling, treating everyone with respect and celebrating wins.

cards.q: "It's not my job" is a great team attitude when it is busy.
cards.why: When it is busy you muck in, even if it is "not your job".

options: Can feel the good atmosphere
Do not notice anything
Have a slower service
Expect lower prices
cards.why: When the team clicks, work is more enjoyable, service is better, and guests can feel the good atmosphere.

cards.q: Reliability is one of the most respected qualities in a team.
cards.why: Colleagues rely on you to turn up on time and ready to work.
